records.implementation: Automated on schedules and triggers: evidence-nightly.yml (cron '17 7 * * *' and '17 19 * * *', plus once after every successful deploy), deploy-with-opa.yml (every push to main, behind the prod approval), zap-dast.yml (weekly, cron '23 7 * * 1'), the runtime emitter on its EventBridge schedule (aws_cloudwatch_event_rule.opa_compliance in infrastructure/main.tf, rate(1 day) from var.compliance_check_schedule) and the evidence watchdog (aws_cloudwatch_event_rule.evidence_watchdog in infrastructure/watchdog.tf, rate(1 hour)). Detection, evaluation (policies/triage.rego via OPA), gating, signing and publication are all automated; the nightly publishes its outcome on every run in vdr-status.json.

records.implementation: policies/triage.rego timeframe() reads the Class C matrix from the pinned FedRAMP rules (data.rules ... VDR-TFR-PVR.varies_by_class.c, hash-checked by scripts/_rules.py) by PAIN x IRV x LEV; the deadline runs from the finding's clock start (triage.rego deadline(), item.clock.start_ns), which only a verified mitigation moves (scripts/build-vdr-report.py clock_facts()); re-evaluation re-selects the timeframe; G3 'vdr.past-deadline' blocks publication (gate-modes.json mode block); likely-overdue margin (vdr-pain-config.json). The published vdr-report.json carries remediation_due_at per finding.

N1 findings get no timeframe (policies/triage.rego timeframe(): 'null for a level with no timeframe (N1: routine operations)'), yet scripts/vuln-gate.py and reconcile.py invariant (h) still need every finding fixed or dispositioned by an in-force decision with review_by. Both N1 findings (tfsec-AVD-AWS-0162, zap-10036-2) carry decisions DEC-032/DEC-040.
